messages:
anya: Heads up — competitor just announced AutoQuantize. PR: https://example.com/autoquantize. We should decide parity vs differentiation by EOW.

mike: saw it. their cost claims look aggressive. any perf breakdown?

lee: looked at the demo — 8-bit path reduces cost but we saw quality drop on long context (>1k tokens).

sophia: customer ops already got a question from ACME pilot. they want a simple toggle to reduce cost.

jen: Options: (A) ship parity: a cheap-mode toggle that enables aggressive quant & caching, (B) differentiate: preserve quality with hybrid selective-fp for attention, (C) route: add automatic fallback to higher-quality variants.

anya: need impact/effort for each. also SLO risk.

mike: infra estimate: parity toggle (hosted API + console flag) ~2 sprints (kernel + rollout + metrics). selective-fp needs eval and kernel work ~3-4 sprints. routing fallback is smaller infra but bigger config UX work.

lee: quick research note: 8-bit attention causes degradation in long-range coherence. prototype flag we used: `selective_fp_for_attention=true` improved coherence at ~1.2x cost vs pure 8-bit.

jen: minimal safe ship: feature behind account-level feature flag + per-route opt-in + preset telemetry (latency, pass@k on eval set).

sophia: GTM: message should be "cost controls with quality safeguards". customers need clear docs on tradeoffs.

anya: is there a compliance/data angle? Private/Dedicated customers might prefer controls not toggles.

mike: yes — dedicated/private could expose knob but default to safe. hosted can be opt-in for now.

lee: I'll put together a 200-prompt eval focused on long-context and hallucination regressions by EOD.

jen: I'll author an RFC template (owners: mike infra, lee research, sophia comms) and link to backlog.

deploy-bot: infra: created branch `feature/autoquantize-planning` by mike. CI checks queued.

anya: OK — consensus leaning to parity behind flag + strong eval/guardrails. decision formalized in RFC. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

mike: +1 — we'll ship opt-in cheap-mode and iterate based on eval & customer feedback.

lee: will surface exact eval metrics in RFC.

sophia: will draft comms + customer FAQ for pilot.

jen: RFC ETA: today 5pm. ask for review by EOD tomorrow.

anya: if anything changes ping here. meeting if we need to unblock.

sophia: ping 3pm sync if RFC looks hairy.

anya: done. thanks all!"
